plan.chapterName: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 24: Electric Potential
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a simple three-dimensional drawing of two conducting spheres joined by a wire. A large shaded sphere occupies the upper right of the frame, and a much smaller sphere in the same style sits at the lower left, roughly a third of the diameter of the first. Both are drawn with a soft interior highlight and are ringed by plus signs spaced around their surfaces to indicate positive charge. A thin grey curve sags gently between them, running from the left side of the large sphere down to the right side of the small one and standing for the connecting wire. Each sphere carries a black dot at its center with a short arrow drawn from that dot out to the surface: the arrow in the large sphere is labeled 'R1' and points up and to the right, while the one in the small sphere is labeled 'R2' and points down and to the left. Giving the two spheres markedly different radii while charging both positively is what sets up the comparison. The arrangement, held at a common potential by the wire, is used to relate the surface charge density on each sphere to its radius.

elements: large conducting sphere on the upper right, pale bluish lavender with soft white highlight and subtle shaded rim
small conducting sphere on the lower left, same material and shading style as the large sphere
black plus signs distributed over the visible surface/rim of the large sphere to indicate positive charge
black plus signs distributed over the visible surface/rim of the small sphere, visually closer together than on the large sphere in the connected view
thin grey curved conducting wire connecting the upper-right side of the small sphere to the left side of the large sphere
black center dot at the center of the large sphere
black center dot at the center of the small sphere
large-sphere radius arrow from the large sphere center toward the upper-right surface
small-sphere radius arrow from the small sphere center toward the lower-right surface
italic label R1 beside the large radius arrow
italic label R2 beside the small radius arrow
optional common-potential annotation near the wire: V1 = V2 when connected
optional separated-view potential annotations near the two spheres showing unequal potentials when disconnected
surface charge density readout near the selected sphere

interactions.label: Radius ratio R1/R2
interactions.teaches: For connected conducting spheres at one potential, the smaller radius sphere has the larger surface charge density; the density ratio grows in direct proportion to R1/R2

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The conducting wire enforces V1 = V2; without the wire, the spheres need not share a common potential and the charge pattern no longer follows the same inverse-radius relation
Selecting either sphere focuses attention on that sphere's radius and local charge density, making the comparison between large R and small surface charge crowding explicit

demo_steps.title: Connected unequal spheres
demo_steps.narration: The wire joins the two positively charged conducting spheres, so the potentials equalize: V1 = V2. The smaller sphere shows more crowded plus signs because its surface charge density is higher.

demo_steps.title: Increase the size contrast
demo_steps.narration: As R1/R2 increases, the small sphere becomes much smaller relative to the large one. In the connected view, the charge density ratio follows σ2/σ1 = R1/R2, so the plus signs crowd more strongly on the small sphere.

demo_steps.title: Disconnect the wire
demo_steps.narration: With the wire removed, the common-potential condition is no longer enforced. The potential labels separate, showing that equalization is a consequence of the conducting connection.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a mostly front-facing 2.5D layout matching the source. World-space layout: +X is screen-right, +Y is screen-up, +Z comes out of the page. Large sphere center at approximately (2.25, 0.75, 0), default radius R1 = 1.10 world units. Small sphere center at approximately (-2.55, -0.85, 0), default radius R2 = R1 / 2.5 = 0.44 world units. Overall figure spans about X = [-3.1, 3.5], Y = [-1.4, 2.0]. Keep the large sphere upper right and the small sphere lower left for all slider values; change R2 from R1 / ratio while keeping R1 fixed. Large radius arrow starts at the large center dot and points about 45 degrees upward-right to the rim; label R1 sits just to the right of the arrow shaft. Small radius arrow starts at the small center dot and slopes downward-right toward the lower-right rim; label R2 sits just right of the center dot. Wire is a thin grey cubic Bezier curve in the XY plane, behind the spheres: start at small center plus roughly (0.82R2, 0.58R2), control points near (-1.35, 0.35, 0) and (0.55, 1.65, 0), end at large center plus roughly (-0.98R1, 0.20R1). Source colors: sphere base pale lavender-blue #cfd3ec, highlight near white #ffffff, shaded edge #aeb4d5, wire grey #777777, arrows/dots/plus signs black #111111. In the source-like default, show about 13 to 15 plus signs on the large sphere and about 6 to 7 on the small sphere, with the small-sphere signs visibly closer together. Connected-view formulas: set total charge Qtotal = 1 in arbitrary units, q1 = R1/(R1 + R2), q2 = R2/(R1 + R2), V1 = V2 = kQtotal/(R1 + R2), and surface density σ = q/(4πR^2), so σ2/σ1 = R1/R2. Separated-view comparison may use equal sphere charges q1 = q2 = 0.5, giving V2/V1 = R1/R2 and σ2/σ1 = (R1/R2)^2; label it clearly as a no-wire reference state.
interactionPlan.notes: Render the spheres as shaded SphereGeometry or camera-facing shaded discs with a radial gradient; the important visual is the textbook-style soft spherical shading rather than physical lighting accuracy. Use billboarding SDF text sprites for plus signs so they face the camera and remain legible. Place plus signs on the visible hemisphere/rim with slight random angular jitter but deterministic seeding; when connected, update their count/spacing according to the connected charge-density relation while preserving the source-like ring distribution. When the connection toggle is separated, fade or remove the grey wire and update the potential labels and charge-density readouts. Clicking a sphere should highlight its outline, center dot, radius arrow, radius label, and readout in a warm accent such as #ff9900 while dimming the other sphere slightly.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for radius ratio R1/R2: the learner changes the relative sphere sizes, the plus signs redistribute more densely on the smaller sphere while the wire keeps both at one potential, showing the inverse relationship between radius and surface charge density.
- Toggle between common-potential and separated-spheres views: the learner connects or disconnects the wire, the potential labels equalize only when connected and the charge pattern updates, making clear what the conducting wire enforces.
